stem: An analyst must establish that one account failed authentication on the VPN, then succeeded, then immediately accessed a file server and triggered an endpoint alert. The three sources store logs separately in different formats. Which capability makes this reconstruction practical?

options.text: Log aggregation into a SIEM, normalising events from all sources into one searchable, time-aligned store
options.why: Aggregation and normalisation are what make a cross-source timeline possible at all. Without them the analyst is manually reconciling three formats and three clocks.

options.text: Alert tuning on the endpoint platform
options.why: Tuning reduces noise from one source. It does not bring three sources together.

options.text: Archiving the logs to long-term storage
options.why: Archiving preserves data for retention. It does not normalise or correlate it.

options.text: Running a vulnerability scan across the three systems
options.why: A scan reports weaknesses that exist, not a sequence of events that happened.

stem: An organisation retains security logs for 30 days. Industry figures put its likely time to detect an intrusion at several months. What is the consequence?

options.text: By the time a breach is detected the evidence of how it began will already have been discarded
options.why: Retention has to exceed realistic detection time or the investigation starts after the record ends. This is why archiving is a named activity rather than housekeeping.

options.text: None, provided the SIEM correlates events in real time
options.why: Real-time correlation catches what the rules recognise. Everything they missed is what you need the history for.

options.text: Detection will be faster because there is less data to search
options.why: Search performance is an engineering problem. Deleting evidence does not improve detection.

options.text: Alert tuning will compensate for the short retention
options.why: Tuning changes which alerts fire now. It cannot recover data already deleted.

stem: A network team needs to be notified immediately when a switch interface goes down or a device reboots unexpectedly. Which mechanism is designed for this?

options.text: SNMP traps sent by the device to the management station
options.why: A trap is the device pushing an unsolicited notification the moment a condition occurs, which is the difference from polling, where the manager asks on a schedule.

options.text: NetFlow records
options.why: NetFlow describes traffic conversations: who talked to whom, how much, for how long. It says nothing about device health.

options.text: A vulnerability scanner
options.why: Enumerates weaknesses on a schedule. It is not an event notification mechanism.

options.text: SCAP content
options.why: SCAP standardises how configuration and vulnerability state is expressed for automated checking.

stem: The objectives distinguish monitoring of systems, applications and infrastructure. Which concern belongs specifically to application monitoring?

options.text: Transaction errors, authentication failures and unusual request patterns within the application itself
options.why: Application monitoring sees what the application does and what its users do inside it, which no layer beneath it can observe.

options.text: CPU, memory and disk utilisation on the host
options.why: That is system monitoring: the operating system and its resources.

options.text: Switch interface errors and link saturation
options.why: Infrastructure monitoring, covering the network and facility layer.

options.text: Whether endpoint agents are installed and reporting
options.why: Agent health sits with system and endpoint monitoring.

stem: A security team must assess laptops that are frequently off the corporate network and rarely connected during scheduled scan windows. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Agent-based scanning, where the agent assesses locally and reports when connectivity allows
options.why: The agent travels with the device and does not depend on the asset being reachable at a particular moment, which is the whole trade-off against agentless.

options.text: Agentless network scanning on a tighter schedule
options.why: More frequent scans still only see devices that happen to be connected. The laptops remain invisible.

options.text: SNMP polling of each laptop
options.why: SNMP is for network and infrastructure device state and is not how endpoints are assessed for vulnerabilities.

options.text: Reviewing NetFlow for the laptops' traffic
options.why: Flow data shows conversations, not patch or configuration state.

stem: A DLP rule matches an outbound message containing customer records. The organisation wants the message held for review rather than blocked outright or delivered. Which response is this?

options.text: Quarantine
options.why: Quarantine holds the item pending a decision, which is the middle path between blocking, which breaks legitimate work, and alerting only, which lets the data leave.

options.text: Alert tuning
options.why: Tuning adjusts which conditions raise an alert. It is not a response action applied to a matched item.

options.text: Archiving
options.why: Archiving moves records to long-term storage. It is not an interception action.

options.text: Remediation validation
options.why: That confirms a fix actually worked, after the fact.

stem: A monthly report shows alert volumes, mean time to triage and the proportion of alerts closed as false positives. What is this reporting principally for?

options.text: Showing whether the monitoring capability itself is healthy and where tuning is needed
options.why: Reporting at this level measures the function rather than any one incident. A rising false positive rate is the signal that tuning is overdue.

options.text: Detecting active intrusions
options.why: Detection happens through alerting in near real time. A monthly summary is far too late for that.

options.text: Satisfying evidence requirements for chain of custody
options.why: Chain of custody documents handling of specific evidence in an investigation.

options.text: Replacing the need for alert tuning
options.why: It indicates that tuning is needed. It does not perform it.

stem: An organisation wants its scanners, configuration tools and reporting to express system state in a common machine-readable format so results can be compared across vendors. Which standard addresses this?

options.text: SCAP
options.why: The Security Content Automation Protocol standardises how vulnerabilities, configuration state and benchmarks are expressed, so different tools produce comparable output.

options.text: NetFlow
options.why: A format for traffic flow records, not for configuration or vulnerability state.

options.text: SNMP
options.why: A protocol for monitoring and managing network devices, not a content standard for security findings.

options.text: SIEM
options.why: A category of product that collects and correlates events, not a standard for expressing state.

stem: Which TWO statements about a security monitoring pipeline are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Correlation is what turns many events from different sources into a single actionable alert
options.why: Aggregation puts data in one place; correlation is the stage that produces meaning from it.

options.text: Retention must exceed realistic time to detect, or evidence is gone before the investigation starts
options.why: Archiving decisions directly bound what any future investigation can establish.

options.text: A high false positive rate is harmless because analysts can ignore those alerts
options.why: It is the main cause of real alerts being missed, which is why tuning is a named activity.

options.text: Aggregation and correlation are two names for the same stage
options.why: One collects and normalises; the other applies rules across what was collected.

options.text: Monthly reporting is the primary mechanism for detecting intrusions
options.why: Reporting measures the function over time. Detection is near real time.
